headline: The classical weak maximum principle for subsolutions of the heat equation on a bounded domain of R^n is fully formalized and kernel-checked UNCONDITIONALLY: no sorry, no axiom, no unsafe, no native_decide, no proof_wanted, and no residual named hypothesis.
summary: Definitions of the parabolic cylinder and parabolic boundary of Omega x (0,T], and of classical subsolutions of u_t - Delta u <= 0; the complete textbook u - eps*t proof (strict core step plus perturbation reduction), with the two one-variable analytic lemmas proved from Mathlib's mean value theorem and Fermat theorem; plus the required kernel-checked finite-dimensional semidiscrete (ODE) comparison lemma in cooperative, discrete-Laplacian and matrix forms. 23/23 audited declarations depend only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

1_definitions.parabolic_cylinder: parabolicCylinder Omega T = closure Omega x Icc 0 T
1_definitions.parabolic_boundary: parabolicBoundary Omega T = parabolicCylinder Omega T \ (Omega x Ioc 0 T); parabolicBoundary_eq gives ((closure Omega \ Omega) x Icc 0 T) union (closure Omega x {0}) for 0 <= T
1_definitions.subsolution: IsHeatSubsolutionOn Omega T u := Nonempty (HeatSubsolutionData Omega T u); data carry one-sided time derivative on Icc 0 t, two-sided first/second spatial derivatives along Function.update coordinate lines, and td - sum gxx <= 0
1_definitions.two_sided_bridge: IsHeatSubsolutionOn.of_classical (classical C^{2,1} formulation: two-sided on Omega x (0,T), left at t = T) and IsHeatSubsolutionOn.of_twoSided (stronger two-sided-everywhere variant)

2_full_classical_proof.note: no narrowly-scoped hypothesis was needed: the second-derivative test at a local maximum and the one-sided derivative bound at an endpoint maximum were both proved from Mathlib's mean value theorem (exists_deriv_eq_slope), Fermat's theorem (IsLocalMax.deriv_eq_zero, IsLocalMaxOn.hasFDerivWithinAt_nonpos) and eventually_nhdsWithin_sign_eq_of_deriv_pos
